Return to the Park.
Dec 2023 • Couples
As with each of our stays in Saigon, we return with pleasure to Au Parc in this restaurant which must have once been a factory, decorated with care having preserved its metal beams and exposed bricks and old tiles.

You can also choose your dishes from the menu of the adjoining Propaganda restaurant. Yesterday we tried the Caesar Salad, well garnished and hearty enough for lunch.
The boss and servers are attentive; the stick of butter and fresh bread to keep you waiting are a plus.

Was this supposed to be a joke or something?
Nov 2023 • Solo
I come to Saigon about two or three times a year. And whenever I do, I ALWAYS eat at Au Parc. Often twice a day. Their roasted Greek salads are great. And I always have avocado and chicken added. Chicken skewers? Perfect! Chicken wrap? Perfect! The staff and the service? Could not be better! They are always so attentive and willing to help out any way they can.
On Saturday evening November 4, I dropped in again for another delicious dinner. A roasted Greek salad with avocado, Diet Coke and their great baguettes with butter. 
After dinner, I asked the waiter if I could order two pork Banh Mi's to go. I was flying home the next morning to San Francisco and I wanted to put them in the fridge at the hotel that night and then take them with me on the long flight home the next morning. 
The waiter was very gracious, and brought them out and showed me that they had wrapped each banh mi in foil, and put them in a plastic container with napkins for the long journey. I was very appreciative.
The next day, at 33,000 feet somewhere abeam Hong Kong, I unwrapped the first banh mi, and couldn't believe what I was holding. It was a bread roll. Period. Nothing in it, and the bread wasn't even sliced in order to put anything in it. 
How can this be? I thought. 
So I took out the second banh mi, opened it up, unwrapped it, and once again a roll with nothing inside. It wasn't even cut open. 
Was this a joke? I wondered. Was the chef trying to prank somebody in the kitchen and messed it up and left the empty rolls in my takeout containers by mistake?
I have no idea.
I thought of calling the restaurant at my intermediate stop in Tokyo, but I figured the person who would answer the phone probably wouldn't have any idea what I was talking about. So instead, I'm writing this review and hoping that it gets somebody's attention.

Pat Palazzolo, 
Fremont, California USA
Read more
Written November 5, 2023
Noelle C
Dear Pat, thank you for your support through the years. I would like to ask how much you were charged fro the banh mi? I am certain that is was not a prank (no one in out team has a sense of humour) but just a misunderstanding. Banh mi means "bread" as well as "filled sandwich" in Vietnam (as I am sure you know if you are a frequent visitor). If you were charged 12.000VND/banh mi, it is because the server misunderstood you (and thought you just wanted bred). If you were charged any more, I need to chop a head so please let me know (this now is humour)! You can write to me directly. noelle@propagandabistros.com Thanks for your time.

Our regular haunt has maintained standards
Jun 2020
This was a restaurant that we frequented about 1-2 times weekly when we used to live a 15 minute walk away, but no longer. Our patronage intervals of this place has dropped to a miserable 2-3 times annually, since we moved further out of time. Tonight, we were ashamedly stuck for a place to eat so what better than to re-visit our old flame.

Au Parc is a Mediterranean restaurant with a loyal bevy of fans. For a rainy Saturday night, these fans were either no longer with them, or just absent, leaving us as the only customers in the restaurant at 7pm on a Saturday evening.

The waiters are extremely pleasant as always, refreshing to see a pleasant face when you are tired and hungry. I ordered the hummus as a shared starter, my wife had a grilled salmon and I had the grilled chicken breast.

Almost immediately after our orders were taken, the waiter plonked a bread basket onto out table followed by our hummus started a few minutes later. The main courses arrived no more than 10 minutes after. As usual, food standards are extremely high at this place, from the quality of the complimentary bread, then the hummus starter and the main courses.

I must also mention that they do fabulous starters here. Prices are reasonable for the quality if food that you get.

Highly recommended obviously!

May 2017 • Solo
Visited Au Parc Saigon for dinner a few days ago. I was in town and had a few hours to kill, so decided to check out this place.

Au Parc Saigon is located in 23, Han Thuyen Street, which is one of the small streets branching off from the Saigon Notre-Dame Basilica. Location is central, easily accessible, and being on a small street with a park in front of it, there isn't the usual noise and smog.

Au Parc Saigon is a bistro style eatery and located right next to Propaganda Bistro, and I believe both are under the same ownership. There's a big "mirror" in the dining area near the main entrance, that on closer look, turned out not to be a mirror at all - it was a glass window looking into Propaganda Bistro! If only it were a one way mirror ..... ;)

I had a rather simple dinner: the Jericho Salad and the Baby Potatoes Sauteed in Olive Oil. I had wanted to have the Shish Kebabs instead of the potatoes, but the girl taking the order was quite adamant that it would be too much as the portions were supposed to be quite big - her insistence has earned my eternal gratitude! And it was extremely refreshing NOT to have a waiter making "recommendations" to me one after another! Au Parc Saigon has a new fan and it's down to her. Unfortunately, I did not get her name, but she was kinda small size, wear glasses and was initially sitting behind the cashier counter.

Cindy Kaw
Dear Amiga007, 

First of all I'm very sorry for the poor experience at our restaurant. 
We do not serve breakfast after 11, but if you ask for it, we can usually find a way around it except during the most complicated time of the year in Vietnam when management becomes a headache because 100% of our suppliers are closed around us (TET holidays). Note that Au Parc is opened throughout the TET period and that most items ont he menu are still available. 80% of restaurants in Saigon close for 3 to 7 days.
However our waiters and assistants are trained to please you ANYWAY. The salmon and spinach should have been hot and the cakes should have been good.
I am not sure what happened about the sugar as it is customary for Vietnamese people to use just as much sugar in their coffee! Perhaps a slight cultural misunderstanding? Vietnamese people laugh when they are scared for example. Perhaps the waiter was surprise to see a "white face" ask for so much sugar?

Again we are very sorry and if one day you decide to come back in the area, feel free to contact us info@auparcsaigon.com

I have lived in HCMC for 8 years and have been coming to and ordering from Au Parc regularly in this time. Why I love it: 
1.Great downtown location but pleasant views over the tree-lined streets near the Cathedral. 
2. Huge Mediterranean menu with choices that would suit anyone- vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, you name it! A regularly changing Specials board gives an even wider range of creative choices. There are also very original dishes on the menu, such as Turkish and North African food, all very tasty and well prepared.
3. All the food is freshly cooked/prepared and the quality is consistent. 
4. Service is generally efficient and competent although sometimes staff have issues with comprehension- be sensitive, they are working through foreign language and in the main, do a good job
5. Prices have remained reasonable compared with similar restaurants
6. Fabulous weekend brunch selections- perfect for that post-party mood, or friends visiting
7 Perfect choice for business, friends, couples,breakfast, lunch and dinner. Really, it ticks all the boxes and the delivery is also fast and efficient. 

The only time I had an issue with anything was when I ordered the mezze and they were cold and bland from having sat too long in the chill cabinet. I found that off-putting, but others might not. 

When ordering delivery, be aware that some of the portion sizes seem small. The "Open sandwiches" are quite expensive because of the ingredients but there is only one layer of bread so it is lighter and smaller. Hungry people should choose a different kind of sandwich! Delivery also comes in a HUGE brown paper bag with a plastic tray inside. It seems rather wasteful and the huge bag looks rather empty when you look inside!

Au Parc is probably one of the most popular restaurants in downtown Saigon so booking for any meal these days is essential. Upstairs is non-smoking. Long may it thrive!

Superb Choice and Value
Oct 2012 • Couples
We came across Au Parc quite by accident. We noticed the French look façade with umbrellas, tables and chairs out front and decided to check it out. Taking an inside downstairs table around 12 noon it was only minutes before this popular ex-pat café was filled to the brim with happy diners.

There are several seating sections – down stairs is fairly small but there are two more levels upstairs including a bright sunny yellow mezzanine with more relaxed seating options, and a first floor level with lots more tables and chairs.

The food is a French-Vietnamese fusion (think French without all the butter and fat, and with an emphasis on really fresh ingredients). With quite an extensive menu, there’s also daily choice with ever changing blackboard specials – all at reasonable prices.

My husband had the chicken salad special of the day and I have the Warm Goats Cheese Salad with Cumin beetroot and fresh orange (160,000 Dong, about AU$7.50) which was delicious and had delectable little croutons with warm (French) grilled goats brie oozing over the edges. Divine. We also ordered fresh juices – mine a Carrot, Apple and Ginger juice (60,000 or AU$3) was as fresh as you can get. 

The special thing about Au Parc is that they bake their own breads on the premises, and they get it right – very French baguette style, and simply the best bread I’ve had out of France. Naturally bread comes complimentary with any order, along with a couple of pats of fine butter.

Au Parc does also offer a wide range of sandwiches (baguettes, wraps and bagels) as well as more substantial mains (including kebabs, steaks, pasta and fish) and they have a list of home-made cakes and desserts that would make any sweet tooth cry. Coupled with a fine selection of teas and what smelled like excellent coffee, Au Parc is the perfect place to take a break from the hustle and bustle of Ho Chi Minh City and enjoy some of the finer things in life.

And if you can’t get in here or are looking for a great dinner option then ask for the card to their sister restaurant The Refinery – without the map on the back you’re unlikely to find it – but it’s well worth the extra effort!

Eat Saigon: Au Parc
Dec 2011 • Friends

Au Parc is another one of my favorite hangouts in the town area. I went there 3 times during my stay in Saigon. It's located in a colonial french shophouse with high ceilings (i love these shophouse features), full of light and life and of course good food. 

Like many restaurants in Saigon or Vietnam, Au Parc does a Mediterranean as well as some French food and some American/English. This is typical of most cafes in Saigon in order to cater to the expats working in Saigon. 

There are 3 different spaces for dining. The ground level is bistro-style. You can watch the preparation of your food along with the madness of the service stuff during rush hour. That or take a seat outside, al fresco style and watch the world scoot by (literally). 

The 1st floor has a Mediterranean section. Really cosy space and very Middle Eastern. What i love about this space is the natural light that falls in from the roof and how it reflects off the yellow walls to create that warmth that envelops the space. Bright and cheery. :) It's amazing how all the contrasting designs, patterns, colors, shapes and textures come together so well. Love the mosaic tiled table tops! 

The bagel is the best i've ever had and this trumps anything we have in Sg. Seriously we've been eating crap all these while. Starbucks bagel is like a rock compared to this. I honestly have no idea how they can create such an airy texture and yet maintain the chewiness of a bagel. Even the ones i had in NYC weren't like that. I'm not too sure what exactly should the texture be- dense and chewy? Or light and chewy? Any bagel expert out there please do enlighten us.

Anyhow, they are so generous with the cheese and it's really good and light cream cheese with a tinge of sourness and saltiness. Beats the lousy Philadelphia cream cheese that we usually get. We had a side order of jam and it's made from mulberry. How exotic right? Fragrant and with the right amount of sweetness. It's certainly not as sour as the usual fresh raspberry or blueberry jam.

This would be a perfect place for a wedding luncheon. This is what i'd call a positive space.

Went back a second time for lunch after visiting Cu Chi Tunnels. I wanted to try their quiche but they didn't make any the day i went. So it was a different sorta bagel for me. Bacon with melted Camembert and rockets. This is absolutely awesome. I was surprised at how full i felt after a half of my bagel even though it is really small.

After a glass of fresh mocha and my bagel, i decided that i should still stuff myself with desserts! This is the only downside to dining alone- there's no one to share my food with and i can't have a variety of dishes for tasting! :(( Anyway, i didn't try the Nemesis Chocolate Cake (it looks like a chocolate truffle block) but it comes highly recommended by Z and i trust her taste in desserts since we essentially have the same tummies.

The cheesecake looks fabulous too but certainly too rich for my overly expanded tummy.

I chose the Earl Grey Creme Brulee because it looks small enough and i love tea/coffee desserts. It certainly didn't disappoint. Very thick pudding, creamy too. I'm not sure what is the perfect texture because i'm not a Creme Brulee fan but it tastes ok to my picky tongue. :P

Z and i went back on the last day of our trip for lunch. Gave the dip a shot because it has spinach and blue cheese and some other cheese in it! Yums. I love the pungent and saltiness of blue cheese but this isn't too overpowering. I was surprised by how refreshing the dip is. 

My drink was practically a dessert in itself. It's a Strawberry banana muesli honey smoothie. High calorie drink! 

The apple crumble is to die for. Extremely soft and melt-in-your-mouth apple slices (not chunks) accompanied by the buttery and crispy crumble and real vanilla ice cream! Vanilla ice cream is only real if they come with vanilla beans. The ice cream is a tad too sweet though but well desserts are meant to be sweet

I was craving for some toasted focaccia and this satisfied my taste buds. Ham cheese and avocado sandwich. The saltiness of the ham is complemented by the creamy avocado and this made in heaven pair is sandwiched between the buttery focaccia. -sighs in contentment- Ok now i'm craving for this. Think it'd have to be Toast for breakfast. 

I would really love to be back for the quiche. I'm sure they do their pastries well. The menu is pretty extensive and it'd take at least 2-3 weeks to taste everything? Or perhaps longer since i already have my favorites. Do check it out if you are in Saigon.

Perhaps the only decent western food in HCMC
I love this place, though sitting outside is waaaay too hot. Sneak inside and enjoy the bliss of air-conditioned loveliness.

The food is fresh, well prepared and - occasionally - quite adventurous. If you're a wimpy westerner like me you won't find any unpleasant fish sauce surprises here, but my Viet Kieu girlfriend assures me the food has a Vietnamese twist which she quite enjoys.

Staff are young, cheeky and prone to lecturing you when you divert from what they consider to be 'your normal order'. But they're also huge fun and very attentive. The guy who parks your motorbike can be trusted not to scratch it - almost uniquely in my experience of downtown bike-parkers.

All in all, for a relaxing, tasty and not-bank-breaking meal followed by a gentle stroll back through the traffic fumes to the heart of Sai Gon, an afternoon or evening meal at Au Parc is quite a treat. I'm not telling you that the breakfasts are any good because I enjoy peace and quiet with my morning coffee :-)
